question.worked_solution:
First, note that the denominator's conjugate is $\sqrt{2} - 1.$

Now, to rationalize the denominator, we multiply both the numerator and denominator by the conjugate $\sqrt{2} - 1,$ and simplify:

$$
\begin{aligned}\frac{2-\sqrt{2}}{\sqrt{2}+1} & = \\ \frac{2-\sqrt{2}}{\sqrt{2}+1}\cdot \frac{\sqrt{2}-1}{\sqrt{2}-1} & = \\ \frac{(2-\sqrt{2})(\sqrt{2}-1)}{(\sqrt{2}+1)(\sqrt{2}-1)} & = \\ \frac{2\sqrt{2}-2-(\sqrt{2})^{2}+\sqrt{2}}{(\sqrt{2})^{2}-(1)^{2}} & = \\ \frac{2\sqrt{2}-2-2+\sqrt{2}}{2-1} & = \\ \frac{2\sqrt{2}-4+\sqrt{2}}{1} & = \\ 3\sqrt{2}-4\end{aligned}
$$
